newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey says north Iraq pullout almost over.
newsitem.headline: Turkey says north Iraq pullout almost over.

text.p: Turkey said on Thursday most of its forces had withdrawn from northern Iraq after a six-week campaign against Kurdish rebels that angered the Arab world.
"We have pulled back into Turkey, leaving a small amount behind," army spokesman Colonel Suleyman Canpolat told reporters in the Turkish city of Diyarbakir.
Turkey sent some 10,000 troops into northern Iraq on May 14 against Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) rebels who use bases in the mountains there to strike into Turkey.
"We have left soldiers behind to help in the delivery and direction of air and artillery fire. We have some units on the other side of the border," he said.
The officer said troops had killed 3,009 guerrillas for the loss of 113 soldiers in the fighting although Western diplomats say the rebel death toll is exaggerated.

Canpolat said 49 members of an Iraqi Kurdish militia allied to Turkey had also died. Kurdish sources say most of the fighting in recent weeks has been between the PKK and the pro-Ankara Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP).

The Arab League has condemned the operation as a violation of Iraqi territory. Northern Iraq has been under Iraqi Kurdish control since after the end of the 1991 Gulf War but Turkey says a power vacuum there has allowed the PKK to flourish.
A Western air force shields Iraq's Kurds from any attack by Baghdad.
More than 24,000 people have died since 1984 in conflict between the army and the PKK, fighting for Kurdish self-rule in southeast Turkey.
